targetAudience.primary: Research, risk, analytics and governance leaders adopting agents for consequential knowledge work
targetAudience.knowledgeAssumption: The reader understands analytical workflows, evaluation benchmarks, controls, robustness checks and organizational approval.
targetAudience.readerProblem: A completed run with polished artifacts and traceable sources is easily mistaken for a conclusion that has survived alternative explanations.

whyNow: TruthInsightBench reports similar overall scores across four agent scaffolds but a shared gap between strong auditability/novelty and weak control testing, robustness and falsifiability.

externalHook.description: An agent completes the workflow and attaches evidence, yet the conclusion has not been tested against plausible alternatives or perturbations.

coreProposition: Execution competence and trustworthy evidentiary judgment are separate acceptance states; consequential knowledge work should require observed challenge evidence for controls, robustness, falsification and bounded generalization before a polished result becomes organizational authority.

originalValue.description: Separates correct execution from trustworthy evidentiary judgment and scales the required challenge depth by consequence, reversibility and uncertainty.

readerTakeaway: Keep useful completed analysis even when its conclusion is not yet accepted; require observed, not merely proposed, challenge evidence before high-consequence outputs gain organizational authority.

supported: Four studied scaffolds using the same frozen base model have a narrow reported overall score spread and no corrected statistically reliable pairwise winner.
Evidence auditability and novelty are comparatively strong across systems, while control testing, robustness and falsifiability are much weaker.
The evaluator gives no credit for controls or robustness checks that are proposed but not executed.
unsupported: A universal ranking of agent scaffolds
A claim that every agent-generated conclusion is unreliable
A claim that one LLM evaluator is expert-equivalent ground truth
A requirement for costly independent review on every low-risk task
uncertain: Which challenge checks should be mandatory by risk class
How evaluator calibration should age across models and domains

firstPartyRole.rationale: The argument derives from public primary research and remains independently useful without any first-party project.

decisionReason: The controlled same-model comparison supports a bounded acceptance architecture while explicitly avoiding a simplistic scaffold leaderboard.
